title: A price on each year's splicing crews

blocks.text: A telecom's fiber program plans which ring builds to start in which year. Each build has a value for every year it may start in, and needs splicing-crew hours in each of its years of work: started in year $`t`$, build $`i`$ uses $`h_{i,0}`$ hours in $`t`$, $`h_{i,1}`$ in $`t+1`$, and so on. Each year has $`H_y`$ crew hours. Some builds are must-dos. The full model, with $`x_{i,t} \in \{0,1\}`$:
The crew rows are the only rows that tie builds together. The planners want a quick upper bound on the best plan's value, for any set of nonnegative prices $`\mu_y`$ per crew hour.

Write the Lagrangian relaxation of the crew rows first: the bound $`L(\mu)`$ as a formula, and what each build chooses on its own once those rows are priced. Then write `crew_bound(builds, hours, prices)` to return `(bound, plan)`: the value $`L(\mu)`$ and the relaxed plan that reaches it, as a dict from build name to start year (builds not started are left out). `builds[name]` holds `"value"` (start year to value), `"hours"` (hours by year of work, a list) and `"must"` (a bool); `hours` and `prices` are dicts by year, with a price for every year a build can be worked in. When two choices of a build are worth exactly the same, either may be returned.
No solver is needed: about ten lines of plain Python.

cases.says: with every price at zero, each project starts in the year its value is highest, and the bound is the sum of those values
the bound includes the price of every crew hour, so prices too high to start anything leave the bound at the hours' worth
an optional project whose every start is worth less than its priced hours stays out of the plan
a must-do project starts in its least bad year even when every start is worth less than its priced hours
a project's hours are charged in each year it is worked on, not only the year it starts
for any nonnegative prices the bound is at least the value of the best plan that fits the crews

origin.section: Any Nonnegative Prices on the Budget Rows Give an Upper Bound

concepts: without the rows that tie projects together, each project or small group chooses on its own
pricing the complicating rows gives an upper bound for any nonnegative prices
